crop_notes: This is a microbiological growth medium, not a plant or crop.
Alder (Alnus spp.) is grown as a timber and nitrogen-fixing tree in forestry and agroforestry systems.
disease_reason: Sooty mold (Capnodium spp. and related fungi) is a well-documented superficial fungal growth on alder foliage and stems, developing on honeydew secreted by sap-feeding insects such as aphids and psyllids.
Downy mildew of alfalfa caused by Peronospora trifoliorum is a well-documented foliar disease of alfalfa.
Stemphylium leaf spot (Stemphylium botryosum) is a recognized foliar disease of alfalfa causing characteristic lesions on leaflets.
Summer black stem and leaf spot caused by Cercospora medicaginis is a well-documented warm-season disease of alfalfa.
Brown rot blossom blight and fruit rot caused by Monilinia laxa/fructicola is a major, well-documented disease of almond.
Refers to the pathogen genus (Stigmina carpophila, cause of shot hole) rather than the disease name, and uses informal 'fungus' phrasing.

crop_notes: Cornus alternifolia, grown as an ornamental landscape tree/shrub.
disease_reason: Names a pathogen genus (Cryptodiaporthe corni causes golden canker on Cornus alternifolia) rather than the disease itself (golden canker).

crop_notes: Heuchera spp.; cultivated as a perennial ornamental (also called coral bells).
disease_reason: Rust caused by Puccinia heucherae is a well-documented foliar disease of Heuchera (alumroot).
This names the fungal pathogen (Stagonospora curtisii, syn. Didymella curtisii) rather than the disease itself, which is properly called red blotch, red fire, or leaf scorch of Amaryllis/Hippeastrum.

crop_notes: Fagus grandifolia; cultivated for timber and as an ornamental shade tree.
disease_reason: Names a fungal pathogen species (Neonectria coccinea) rather than the disease itself; the associated disease on American beech is beech bark disease, typically in a scale-insect/Neonectria complex.

crop_notes: Fagus grandifolia; cultivated for timber and as an ornamental shade tree.
disease_reason: Well-documented emerging disease of American beech caused by the foliar nematode Litylenchus crenatae mccannii, first described in Ohio in 2012 and now widespread in the eastern U.S.
Boxwood blight, caused by Calonectria pseudonaviculata, is a well-documented and economically significant fungal disease of American boxwood (Buxus sempervirens).
Chestnut blight, caused by Cryphonectria parasitica, is the devastating canker disease that decimated American chestnut populations.

crop_notes: Ulmus americana is cultivated as a shade/ornamental tree and historically for timber.
disease_reason: Dutch Elm Disease, caused by Ophiostoma ulmi and O. novo-ulmi, is the most devastating and well-documented vascular wilt disease of American Elm (Ulmus americana).
Disease of American beech (Fagus grandifolia) caused by scale insect and Neonectria fungi, not associated with apple.
Major apple disease caused by Venturia inaequalis affecting leaves and fruit worldwide.
Destructive bacterial disease of apple caused by Erwinia amylovora affecting blossoms, shoots, and branches.
Well-known apple disease caused by Botryosphaeria obtusa causing frogeye leaf spot, fruit rot, and limb cankers.
Classic apple disease caused by Gymnosporangium juniperi-virginianae requiring both apple and juniper hosts.
Important postharvest apple disease caused by Penicillium expansum affecting stored fruit.
Seiridium canker, caused by Seiridium spp. (e.g., S. unicorne, S. cardinale), is a well-documented canker disease of arborvitae (Thuja) and other Cupressaceae.

crop_notes: Refers to Fraxinus spp., cultivated as a timber and ornamental tree.
disease_reason: Ash rust caused by Puccinia sparganioides is a well-documented foliar and shoot disease of Fraxinus species.

crop_notes: Populus species grown for timber, pulpwood, and biomass.
disease_reason: Marssonina spp. (e.g., M. brunnea, M. populi) are well-documented foliar pathogens causing leaf spot and premature defoliation in aspen and poplar.

crop_notes: Populus species grown for timber, pulpwood, and biomass.
disease_reason: Cytospora chrysosperma (Valsa sordida) is a widely reported canker pathogen of aspen and poplar, especially on stressed trees.

crop_notes: Pinus nigra; grown as an ornamental/landscape tree and for timber and windbreaks.
disease_reason: Names the fungal pathogen (Diplodia sapinea) rather than the disease it causes, which is Diplodia tip blight (Sphaeropsis tip blight) of Austrian pine.

crop_notes: Cultivated commercially as a Christmas tree and for timber/pulpwood.
disease_reason: Rhizosphaera kalkhoffii is primarily a pathogen of spruces (especially Colorado blue spruce); it is only occasionally reported on true firs and is an unusual association with balsam fir.

crop_notes: Cultivated commercially as a Christmas tree and for timber/pulpwood.
disease_reason: Uredinopsis spp. cause a well-documented heteroecious rust that alternates between Abies balsamea (needles) and ferns.

Cochliobolus is a pathogen genus (teleomorph of Bipolaris/Drechslera) rather than a specific disease; on barley this typically refers to spot blotch (Cochliobolus sativus) or net blotch, so the label is ambiguous.
Basil downy mildew, caused by Peronospora belbahrii, is a well-documented and economically significant foliar disease of sweet basil worldwide.
Bermudagrass rust caused by Puccinia cynodontis is a well-documented foliar disease of Cynodon dactylon.

Limonomyces (e.g., L. roseipellis) causes pink patch on turfgrasses, but the label names the pathogen genus rather than the disease and is a less common association with bermudagrass than with cool-season turf.
Powdery mildew (caused by Phyllactinia guttata and other Erysiphales) is a well-documented foliar disease of birch.
Marssonina leaf spot is well-known on poplar, willow, and rose; its association with birch is uncommon and not a standard birch disease.

Black knot, caused by Apiosporina morbosa, is a well-documented fungal disease that commonly affects Prunus serotina (black cherry), producing characteristic black, swollen galls on twigs and branches.
Thousand Cankers Disease is a well-documented lethal disease of black walnut (Juglans nigra) caused by the fungus Geosmithia morbida vectored by the walnut twig beetle (Pityophthorus juglandis).
Tobacco Rattle Virus is a well-documented viral pathogen known to infect Bleeding Heart (Dicentra/Lamprocapnos spectabilis), causing ringspot and mosaic symptoms.

crop_notes: Picea pungens, cultivated as an ornamental/Christmas tree.
disease_reason: Almost certainly a misspelling of the pathogen Chrysomyxa weirii (Weir's cushion rust); label names a pathogen rather than a disease and the genus 'Ceropsora' is not valid.

crop_notes: Picea pungens, cultivated as an ornamental/Christmas tree.
disease_reason: Well-documented group of Chrysomyxa rust diseases that affect spruce species, including blue spruce.

crop_notes: Picea pungens, cultivated as an ornamental/Christmas tree.
disease_reason: Rhizosphaera kalkhoffii is a classic and highly prevalent needle cast pathogen of Picea pungens (blue spruce).
Well-documented destructive disease of boxwood caused by Calonectria pseudonaviculata.
Names the pathogen (with taxonomic authority) rather than the disease; the corresponding disease is Volutella blight/canker of boxwood.

Tomato spotted wilt virus (TSWV) is a well-documented tospovirus with a very broad host range that includes Sinningia speciosa (Brazilian gloxinia), causing ringspots, chlorotic blotches, and stunting.
Downy mildew caused by Hyaloperonospora parasitica (syn. Peronospora parasitica) is a well-documented and economically important disease of broccoli and other Brassica crops.

crop_notes: Aesculus spp.; grown ornamentally and for timber, though seeds are toxic if not processed.
disease: Guignardia Blotch Of Buckeyes And Horsechestnuts
disease_reason: Guignardia leaf blotch, caused by Guignardia aesculi, is a well-documented foliar disease of Aesculus species including buckeyes and horsechestnuts.

crop_notes: Light air-cured variety of Nicotiana tabacum grown commercially for cigarette blends.
disease_reason: Blue mold caused by Peronospora tabacina is a major foliar disease of burley tobacco worldwide.

crop_notes: Light air-cured variety of Nicotiana tabacum grown commercially for cigarette blends.
disease_reason: Rhizoctonia solani causes damping-off in float beds and target spot/sore shin on field tobacco including burley.

crop_notes: Light air-cured variety of Nicotiana tabacum grown commercially for cigarette blends.
disease_reason: TSWV (genus Orthotospovirus) is a well-documented thrips-transmitted virus of tobacco causing necrotic ringspots and stunting in burley.
Peronospora parasitica is a well-documented foliar disease of cabbage and other crucifers.
Pectobacterium/Erwinia-induced soft rot is a major postharvest and field disease of cabbage heads.

Phytophthora root/stem rot is not a commonly reported disease of cabbage; crucifers are more typically affected by Phytophthora porri or P. brassicae in rare cases, making this an unusual association.
Xanthomonas campestris pv. campestris black rot is the most important bacterial disease of cabbage worldwide.
Plasmodiophora brassicae clubroot is a classic and devastating soil-borne disease of cabbage.

crop_notes: Composite grouping of three distinct Brassica oleracea crops; should be split or comma-separated rather than combined as one crop name.
disease_reason: Alternaria (A. brassicae/A. brassicicola) causes black/dark leaf spot on brassicas, but 'black molds / stem cankers' is an atypical and imprecise descriptor for this disease on cabbage, collards, and kale.

crop_notes: Genus name; commonly grown as ornamental, though Camellia sinensis is the tea plant (beverage crop).
disease_reason: Phytophthora ramorum does infect Camellia (as a foliar/twig host and major nursery carrier), but the disease name 'Sudden Oak Death' refers to the lethal oak syndrome — on Camellia it is properly called Ramorum blight/dieback.

crop_notes: Genus name; commonly grown as ornamental, though Camellia sinensis is the tea plant (beverage crop).
disease_reason: Well-documented disease of Camellia caused by Ciborinia camelliae, producing brown petal lesions and rapid flower collapse.

crop_notes: Group label covering Rubus cane fruits (blackberry, raspberry).
disease_reason: Orange rust (Arthuriomyces peckianus / Gymnoconia nitens) is a well-documented systemic rust disease of blackberry and black raspberry.
Alternaria can cause black mold on carrot roots in storage, but 'stem cankers' is not a standard carrot disease term and the combined label is vague.
Alternaria leaf blight (Alternaria dauci) is a well-documented and economically important foliar disease of carrot.

Cryptosporiopsis cankers are well-documented on hardwoods (e.g., aspen, oak) but are not a typical or well-established canker disease of Cedar (Cedrus or Thuja); cedar cankers are more commonly attributed to Seiridium, Botryosphaeria, or Kabatina.
Ascochyta blight, caused by Ascochyta rabiei, is one of the most economically important and well-documented fungal diseases of chickpea worldwide.
Rhizoctonia solani is a well-documented soilborne pathogen causing damping-off, wirestem, bottom rot and head rot on Chinese cabbage and other brassicas.
Entomosporium leaf spot, caused by Entomosporium mespili (Diplocarpon mespili), is a well-documented foliar disease of chokeberry (Aronia) and other Rosaceae.
Citrus canker is a well-documented bacterial disease of citrus caused by Xanthomonas citri subsp. citri, producing raised corky lesions on leaves, fruit, and stems.

crop_notes: Native California wild oak; ecologically important and sometimes planted as an ornamental shade tree, but not cultivated as an agricultural or horticultural crop.

disease_reason: Downy mildew caused by Peronospora belbahrii (and related Peronospora spp.) is a well-documented foliar disease of Coleus (Plectranthus scutellarioides) causing leaf yellowing, defoliation, and characteristic sporulation on leaf undersides.
Beet curly top virus (BCTV) is a well-documented leafhopper-transmitted geminivirus that infects common bean, causing curly top disease.
Halo blight, caused by Pseudomonas savastanoi pv. phaseolicola, is a major bacterial disease of common bean.
'Timber rot' is the tomato-specific common name for Sclerotinia sclerotiorum; on common bean this disease is properly called white mold or Sclerotinia stem rot.
Bean rust caused by Uromyces appendiculatus is a well-known fungal disease of common (dry) bean.

disease: Common Bacterial  Blight Of Beans, Fuscous Blight
disease_reason: Common bacterial blight (Xanthomonas axonopodis pv. phaseoli) and fuscous blight (var. fuscans) are the recognized bacterial blights of common bean.
Rhizoctonia solani is a well-documented soilborne pathogen of sugar/common beet causing seedling damping-off, crown/root rot, and foliar blight.

crop_notes: Also known as common hazel (Corylus avellana); cultivated for hazelnuts.
disease_reason: Eastern Filbert Blight, caused by Anisogramma anomala, is a well-documented and economically significant fungal disease of Corylus avellana (Common Filbert/Hazelnut).
Names a fungal genus rather than a specific disease; Cladosporium can cause minor leaf spot on lilac but the label is vague.
Anthracnose is a real disease group but is not a commonly documented or significant disease of common lilac (Syringa vulgaris).

crop_notes: Physocarpus opulifolius, a deciduous shrub widely grown as an ornamental landscape plant.
disease_reason: Powdery mildew (commonly caused by Podosphaera species) is a well-documented and frequently observed foliar disease of Physocarpus opulifolius (common ninebark).
Pear scab caused by Venturia pyrina is a well-documented fungal disease of common pear affecting leaves and fruit.
Bitter rot (Colletotrichum spp.) and anthracnose are real diseases that can affect pear, but bundling two distinct disease names into one label is vague and conflates separate conditions.
Sunflower rust caused by Puccinia helianthi is a well-documented and economically important disease of common sunflower worldwide.

Sclerotinia sclerotiorum does cause head, stalk, and basal rot in sunflower, but 'Timber Rot' is a name typically applied to Sclerotinia stem rot of tomato and is not a standard name for any sunflower disease.
Well-documented rust disease of corn caused by Puccinia polysora.
Vague umbrella term; corn has several distinct bacterial rots/blights that should be named specifically.
Common smut of corn caused by Ustilago maydis is a well-known disease.
Standard rust disease of corn caused by Puccinia sorghi.
Names the pathogen (X. vasicola pv. vasculorum causes bacterial leaf streak of corn) rather than the disease itself.
Major foliar disease of corn caused by Cercospora zeae-maydis.
Goss's bacterial wilt and blight, caused by Clavibacter nebraskensis, is a well-known corn disease.
Well-documented foliar disease of corn caused by Exserohilum turcicum.
Brown spot of corn caused by Physoderma maydis is a recognized disease.

disease: White Ear Rot And Seedling Blight Of Maize
disease_reason: Known disease complex of maize, typically associated with Stenocarpella maydis (Diplodia).
Anthracnose leaf blight and stalk rot of corn is caused by Colletotrichum graminicola.
Names the pathogen species rather than the disease (Gibberella ear/stalk rot of corn).
Several Peronosclerospora spp. cause downy mildews of corn, particularly in tropical regions.

disease: Dry Rot Of Ears And Stalks Of Maize
disease_reason: Diplodia dry rot of ears and stalks (Stenocarpella maydis) is a recognized maize disease.

Brown rot (Monilinia spp.) is primarily a disease of stone fruits (Prunus); while Cornus mas fruits can occasionally develop fungal rots, brown rot is not a well-documented or characteristic disease of Cornelian Cherry Dogwood.
Corynespora leaf spot, caused by Corynespora cassiicola, is a well-documented foliar disease of cotton that produces target-like necrotic lesions on leaves.

Generic symptom-based label rather than a specific named disease; cowpea flowers can be affected by Choanephora blight or Botrytis, but 'Flower Blights' alone is too vague to identify the causal pathogen.

crop_notes: Combined entry grouping crabapple (Malus spp.) with cultivated apple (Malus domestica); should be split or standardised.
disease_reason: Japanese apple rust (Gymnosporangium yamadae) is a well-documented rust disease affecting apple and crabapple (Malus spp.) foliage and fruit.

crop_notes: Agrostis stolonifera; primarily cultivated as a turfgrass for golf greens and lawns rather than forage, but falls under cultivated grass crops.
disease_reason: Anthracnose, caused by Colletotrichum cereale, is a well-documented foliar blight and basal rot disease of creeping bentgrass on golf course greens.

crop_notes: Agrostis stolonifera; primarily cultivated as a turfgrass for golf greens and lawns rather than forage, but falls under cultivated grass crops.
disease_reason: Dollar spot, caused by Clarireedia jacksonii (formerly Sclerotinia homoeocarpa), is one of the most economically important diseases of creeping bentgrass turf.

crop_notes: Pennisetum setaceum 'Rubrum'; grown as an ornamental grass.
disease_reason: Take-all root rot (Gaeumannomyces graminis) primarily affects turfgrasses and cereals; its association with ornamental Crimson Fountaingrass (Pennisetum setaceum 'Rubrum') is not well-documented in standard plant pathology literature.
Pseudoperonospora cubensis is a major downy mildew disease of cucumber and other cucurbits.
Colletotrichum orbiculare causes anthracnose, a well-documented foliar and fruit disease of cucumber.
Pseudomonas syringae pv. lachrymans is the classic bacterial angular leaf spot pathogen of cucumber.
Phytophthora capsici causes crown, fruit, and foliar blight on cucumber and other cucurbits.
Cucurbit scab caused by Cladosporium cucumerinum is a well-known disease of cucumber.
Podosphaera xanthii and Erysiphe cichoracearum are well-documented powdery mildew pathogens of cucumber.
Corynespora cassiicola causes target leaf spot on cucumber, especially in greenhouse production.
Pythium spp. do cause damping-off and root rot on cucumber, but the label names a pathogen genus rather than a specific disease.
Erwinia tracheiphila, vectored by cucumber beetles, causes bacterial wilt of cucumber.
Rhizoctonia solani causes damping-off, belly rot, and foliar blight on cucumber.
Stagonosporopsis cucurbitacearum (formerly Didymella bryoniae) causes gummy stem blight and black rot on cucumber.
Not a disease name; it strings together two fungal genera (Alternaria, Embellisia) and what appears to be a taxonomic authority, though Embellisia allii does cause skin blotch on garlic.
Gray mold / Botrytis neck rot (Botrytis porri, B. allii, B. cinerea) is a well-documented field and storage disease of garlic, though the plural form is imprecise.
Rust caused by Puccinia allii (P. porri) is a well-known foliar disease of garlic and other Alliums, often called garlic/leek/onion rust interchangeably.
Colloquial term for Rhizopus/Neurospora; Rhizopus soft rot of garlic bulbs in storage does exist, but 'bread mold' is not a standard phytopathological disease label.
White rot caused by Stromatinia cepivora (Sclerotium cepivorum) is one of the most destructive soilborne diseases of cultivated garlic.

crop_notes: Rumex crispus is a weedy wild plant, not cultivated as an agricultural or horticultural crop.

disease_reason: Tubercularia canker (caused by Tubercularia spp., anamorph of Nectria) is a documented canker disease affecting Daphne shrubs.

crop_notes: Dark (air- or fire-cured) tobacco is a recognized commercial class of Nicotiana tabacum.
disease_reason: Phytophthora nicotianae causes black shank/Phytophthora blight, a well-documented and economically important disease of dark tobacco.

crop_notes: Refers to dead standing or fallen woody material in forests, not a plant or cultivated crop.
Leucothoe spp., an evergreen shrub used in landscape ornamental horticulture.
disease: Calonectria Cylindrospora Crous, Alfenas & M.J. Wingf.
disease_reason: This is a pathogen species name with taxonomic authors rather than a disease name, and Calonectria cylindrospora is not a well-established pathogen specifically reported on Leucothoe (doghobble).
Powdery mildew (caused primarily by Erysiphe pulchra) is a well-documented foliar disease of flowering dogwood (Cornus florida).
Dogwood anthracnose, caused by Discula destructiva, is a major and well-documented disease of Cornus florida and C. nuttallii.

crop_notes: Refers to double-flowered cultivars of Impatiens, grown as bedding ornamentals.
disease_reason: Downy mildew caused by Plasmopara obducens is a well-documented and devastating disease of Impatiens walleriana including double-flowered cultivars.

crop_notes: Grown as a timber and Christmas tree crop; Pseudotsuga menziesii.
disease_reason: Well-documented foliar disease of Douglas-fir caused by the fungus Nothophaeocryptopus gaeumannii.

crop_notes: Grown as a timber and Christmas tree crop; Pseudotsuga menziesii.
disease_reason: Rhabdocline spp. (e.g., R. pseudotsugae, R. weirii) cause classic needle cast diseases specific to Douglas-fir.

crop_notes: Tsuga canadensis; cultivated as ornamental and managed for timber.
disease_reason: Hemlock tip blight, caused by Sirococcus tsugae, is a well-documented fungal disease affecting Eastern Hemlock (Tsuga canadensis), causing dieback of new shoots and needles.

crop_notes: Juniperus virginiana; cultivated for timber, windbreaks, and ornamental use.
disease_reason: Gymnosporangium juniperi-virginianae forms galls on Eastern Redcedar (Juniperus virginiana) as its telial host in a well-documented heteroecious rust life cycle with apple.
Caliciopsis pinea is a well-documented canker disease of Eastern white pine, especially in the northeastern US.
Needle cast is a real disease category (e.g., white pine needle damage complex involving Lecanosticta, Lophophacidium, Bifusella) but the label is vague and not pathogen-specific.
Cronartium ribicola causes blister rust, the most economically significant disease of Eastern white pine.
Stem rot is not a standard disease name for Eastern white pine; root and butt rots (Heterobasidion, Armillaria) are documented but 'stem rot' is vague and atypical for conifers.
Septoria is a foliar pathogen of broadleaf plants (tomato, hemp, etc.); pines have needles, not leaves, and Septoria is not a recognized pathogen of Eastern white pine.
Leaf blotch is a disease of broadleaf hosts; Eastern white pine has needles, and 'leaf blotch' is not a recognized disease of this conifer.
Names the pathogen (Phomopsis vexans, syn. Diaporthe vexans) with taxonomic authority rather than the disease name 'Phomopsis blight/fruit rot'.
Phytophthora blight (caused by Phytophthora spp., e.g., P. capsici, P. nicotianae) is a well-documented disease of eggplant affecting foliage, stems, and fruit.

crop_notes: Cultivated as an ornamental and timber tree (genus Ulmus).
disease_reason: Classic vascular wilt of elms caused by Ophiostoma ulmi/novo-ulmi, vectored by elm bark beetles.

crop_notes: Cultivated as an ornamental and timber tree (genus Ulmus).
disease_reason: Black spot/anthracnose-type leaf spots (e.g., Stegophora ulmea) do occur on elm, but 'Black Spot of Elm' is not a standard disease name and is more commonly associated with rose.

crop_notes: Cultivated as an ornamental and timber tree (genus Ulmus).
disease_reason: Xylella fastidiosa causes bacterial leaf scorch in elm, producing marginal necrosis and dieback.

crop_notes: Also cultivated as a medicinal herb (horny goat weed) in traditional Chinese medicine.
disease_reason: Tobacco Rattle Virus (TRV) is a well-documented nepovirus-like tobravirus that infects Epimedium, causing characteristic ringspot and mosaic symptoms on foliage.
Septoria betulae and related Septoria species are documented foliar pathogens causing leaf spot on Betula pendula (European birch).
Both are real Colletotrichum-caused diseases of Malus, but bundling two distinct disease names into one label is imprecise and should be split into separate entries.
Real disease category but vague; raspberry rusts include yellow rust (Phragmidium rubi-idaei) and late rust (Pucciniastrum americanum), and the specific pathogen is not identified.
Cane canker caused by Gnomonia species (e.g., Gnomonia rubi) is a documented disease of Rubus idaeus affecting canes.

Ascochyta blight, caused by the Ascochyta/Mycosphaerella complex (Ascochyta pisi, Mycosphaerella pinodes, Phoma medicaginis var. pinodella), is a well-documented and economically important foliar/stem disease of field pea (Pisum sativum).

crop_notes: Ambiguous grouping; edible fig (Ficus carica) is cultivated as a fruit crop, while banyan (Ficus benghalensis) is typically a non-crop shade/ornamental tree.
disease_reason: Fig rust, caused by Cerotelium fici, is a well-documented foliar disease of fig (Ficus carica) causing yellow-brown leaf spots and premature defoliation.

crop_notes: Flue-cured (Virginia) tobacco is a curing-method-defined market class of Nicotiana tabacum grown as a commercial non-food crop.
disease_reason: Tobacco is affected by Phytophthora nicotianae causing black shank (root/stem rot), not typically called 'Phytophthora Blight'; the label is vague and likely refers to black shank.
Phomopsis spp. are well-documented causes of cankers and twig blights on Forsythia, producing dieback and stem lesions.
Aspergillus niger causes black mold, a well-documented postharvest disease of onion bulbs.
Peronospora destructor is a classic, economically important foliar disease of Allium cepa.
Phytoplasma yellows diseases do occur in onion, but the label names the pathogen rather than the disease (e.g., 'onion yellows') and is uncommonly reported as a major onion disease.
Fusarium basal rot is the canonical Fusarium disease of onion; damping-off in onion seedlings is more typically attributed to Pythium, making this association unusual.
IYSV (Tospovirus, thrips-vectored) is a globally significant disease of onion bulb and seed crops.
Alternaria porri causes purple blotch, a major foliar disease of onion.
Geranium rust caused by Puccinia pelargonii-zonalis is a well-documented fungal disease of Pelargonium (geranium).

crop_notes: Invasive shrub, not cultivated as a crop.

disease_reason: Phytophthora capsici causes well-documented blight on cucurbits including gourds, affecting fruit, crowns, and foliage.
Fusarium species are recognized causal agents of damping-off in cucurbit seedlings including gourds.
Powdery mildew caused by Podosphaera xanthii and Erysiphe cichoracearum is a major foliar disease of gourds and other cucurbits.
Caused by Erysiphe necator, a major worldwide grape disease.
Caused by Guignardia bidwellii, a well-known destructive grape disease.
Botrytis cinerea bunch rot is a major grape disease affecting berries and clusters.
Caused by Elsinoe ampelina, a documented disease of grapevines.
Caused by Plasmopara viticola, one of the most important grape diseases globally.
Caused by Pseudocercospora vitis (formerly Mycosphaerella angulata), a recognized grape leaf disease.

crop_notes: Crataegus spp.; grown ornamentally and as hedging, with some species cultivated for edible/medicinal fruit.
disease_reason: Quince rust (Gymnosporangium clavipes) is a well-documented disease of hawthorn (Crataegus spp.), which serves as a common telial host causing fruit and twig deformation.

crop_notes: Cannabis sativa is cultivated for fiber (hemp), oilseed, and medicinal/recreational use (marijuana).
disease_reason: Beet curly top virus (BCTV), transmitted by the beet leafhopper, is a documented and economically significant virus infecting Cannabis sativa, causing leaf curling, stunting, and yield loss.
Names a fungal genus rather than a specific disease, and Ascochyta is not a well-documented pathogen of hickory (Carya spp.).

Downy mildew (Peronospora sparsa) is documented on Rubus species but is far more commonly reported on raspberry and boysenberry than on highbush blackberry, making this an unusual/uncertain association without pathogen specification.
Anthracnose fruit rot caused by Colletotrichum spp. is a well-documented disease of highbush blueberry.
Generic symptom-based label; multiple pathogens cause twig cankers on blueberry, so the specific disease is ambiguous.
Leaf rust caused by Thekopsora minima (formerly Pucciniastrum vaccinii) is a known disease of highbush blueberry.
Phomopsis canker and twig blight caused by Diaporthe vaccinii is a well-documented disease of highbush blueberry.
This names the pathogen (Diaporthe vaccinii Shear) rather than the disease itself, and duplicates the Phomopsis canker entry.
Mummy berry caused by Monilinia vaccinii-corymbosi is a major and well-documented disease of highbush blueberry.
Hollyhock rust caused by Puccinia malvacearum is the most common and well-documented disease of hollyhock (Alcea rosea).

crop_notes: Humulus lupulus; cultivated primarily for brewing beer.
disease: Fusarium Wilts, Blights, Rots And Damping-Off
disease_reason: Fusarium can cause canker/cone tip blight on hops, but this catch-all grouping is vague and not a specific hop disease name.

crop_notes: Humulus lupulus; cultivated primarily for brewing beer.
disease_reason: Carnation latent virus is a carnation-infecting carlavirus and is not a recognized pathogen of hops.

crop_notes: Humulus lupulus; cultivated primarily for brewing beer.
disease_reason: Apple mosaic virus (ApMV) is a well-documented ilarvirus of hops causing hop mosaic-like symptoms and yield/alpha-acid losses.

crop_notes: Humulus lupulus; cultivated primarily for brewing beer.
disease_reason: Hop powdery mildew caused by Podosphaera macularis is a major, well-documented disease of hops worldwide.

crop_notes: Humulus lupulus; cultivated primarily for brewing beer.
disease_reason: Cucurbit downy mildew (Pseudoperonospora cubensis) infects cucurbits; hops have their own downy mildew caused by P. humuli, so this label is the wrong host.
Sclerotium rolfsii (Athelia rolfsii) is a well-documented soilborne pathogen causing crown and petiole rot in hostas, especially in warm, humid conditions.
Hosta Virus X (HVX), a potexvirus, is the signature and most economically important viral disease of Hosta, causing mottling, ink-bleed patterns, and tissue collapse.
Tobacco rattle virus (TRV), vectored by Trichodorus/Paratrichodorus nematodes, is a documented infector of Hosta producing ringspots, line patterns, and chlorotic mottling.
Cercospora leaf spot (Cercospora hydrangeae) is a real and common hydrangea disease, but the label names the pathogen genus rather than the disease itself.
Gray mold (Botrytis cinerea) does affect hydrangea blossoms and shoots, but the pluralized, informal phrasing is vague and non-standard.
Heterosporium leaf spot (caused by Heterosporium iridis, now Mycosphaerella macrospora / Cladosporium iridis) is a well-documented foliar disease of Iris.

Phyllosticta species are typically associated with broadleaf hosts; on Italian Cypress (a conifer with scale-like leaves), needle/twig blights (e.g., Seiridium, Pestalotiopsis, Cercospora) are far more commonly reported than Phyllosticta leaf spots.

Tar spot needlecast, caused by Lophodermium species (notably L. pinastri), is a documented foliar disease of Jack Pine (Pinus banksiana) producing black ascocarps on needles and premature needle cast.
Hypocrea is a fungal genus (teleomorph of Trichoderma), not a specific disease name, and is generally not a primary pathogen of Japanese flowering cherry.
Anthracnose (caused by Discula, Colletotrichum, or Aureobasidium spp.) is a well-documented foliar disease of Acer palmatum causing leaf blotches and shoot dieback.
Phomopsis spp. are recognized causal agents of cankers and twig blight on stressed Japanese maples, particularly following winter or drought injury.
Powdery mildew (commonly Sawadaea spp. and other Erysiphales) is a documented foliar disease of Japanese maple, producing the characteristic white surface mycelium on leaves.
Cronartium ribicola requires a Ribes host (including Jostaberry, a Ribes hybrid) to complete its life cycle and causes leaf rust symptoms on it.
Names a pathogen species (the teleomorph of Phomopsis juniperovora) rather than a disease, and duplicates the Phomopsis entry.
Well-documented juniper twig blight caused by Kabatina juniperi affecting previous-year shoots.
Vague generic term; needle cast diseases are characteristic of true-needled conifers (pine, spruce, fir) rather than scale-leaved junipers.
Pestalotiopsis is typically a weak/opportunistic pathogen on juniper causing tip blight rather than a classical leaf spot, and the association is minor.
Phomopsis juniperovora is the classic and economically important tip blight/canker disease of juniper, especially on young growth.
Leptosphaerulina leaf blight is well-documented on forage legumes (alfalfa, clover) and turfgrasses, but is not a commonly recognized or well-documented disease of kale (Brassica oleracea).

crop_notes: Poa pratensis; widely cultivated as turfgrass and pasture forage.
disease_reason: Spring Dead Spot is a well-documented disease of warm-season turfgrasses (especially bermudagrass), not a typical disease of cool-season Kentucky Bluegrass.

crop_notes: Poa pratensis; widely cultivated as turfgrass and pasture forage.
disease_reason: Names a pathogen genus rather than the disease; the proper disease name on Kentucky Bluegrass is Ascochyta leaf blight.

crop_notes: Poa pratensis; widely cultivated as turfgrass and pasture forage.
disease_reason: Wheat stem rust (Puccinia graminis f. sp. tritici) is a disease of wheat and related cereals, not Kentucky Bluegrass.

crop_notes: Generic term for turfgrass species used in lawns; should be written as two words.
disease_reason: Rust diseases caused by Puccinia spp. (e.g., P. graminis, P. coronata, P. striiformis) are well-documented fungal diseases affecting turfgrasses/lawn grasses.
Green mold caused by Penicillium digitatum is a major postharvest disease of lemons and other citrus fruits.
Not a standard disease name in citrus pathology; likely a colloquial reference to the whisker-like sporulation of Penicillium spp. on lemons, overlapping with green/blue mold.
Ascochyta blight, caused by Ascochyta lentis, is a well-documented and economically important foliar disease of lentil worldwide.
Caused by Bremia lactucae, a major and well-documented foliar disease of lettuce worldwide.
Erysiphe cichoracearum causes powdery mildew on lettuce, particularly in greenhouse and field crops.
Sclerotinia sclerotiorum causes lettuce drop / stem rot, a classic and economically important disease of lettuce.
'Timber rot' is the common name for Sclerotinia on tomato; on lettuce the same pathogen is normally called 'lettuce drop,' so this name is unusual and overlaps with Sclerotinia Stem Rot.
Botrytis cinerea commonly infects lettuce, causing gray mold especially on senescing tissue and in cool, humid conditions.
Cercospora longissima can affect lettuce in warm, humid regions, but it is an uncommon and minor disease and the label names a pathogen genus rather than a specific disease.
LCV (Crinivirus) is a recognized whitefly-transmitted virus of lettuce causing interveinal yellowing.
MiLBVV (Ophiovirus), vectored by Olpidium brassicae, is the causal agent of lettuce big-vein disease.
Rhizoctonia solani causes damping-off, bottom rot, and web blight on lettuce, all well documented.
TSWV (thrips-transmitted Tospovirus) has a broad host range including lettuce, causing necrotic spots and stunting.
Sclerotium rolfsii (Athelia rolfsii) causes southern blight on lettuce in warm regions, producing crown rot and white mycelial mats.
Seiridium canker (caused by Seiridium unicorne and related species) is the most well-documented and damaging canker disease of Leyland cypress.

Anthracnose is not a commonly documented disease of lilac (Syringa spp.); lilacs are far more typically affected by bacterial blight (Pseudomonas syringae) and powdery mildew, making this an unusual association.

crop_notes: Pinus flexilis is a wild high-elevation conifer, not cultivated as an agricultural or horticultural crop.
Quercus virginiana; cultivated as an ornamental/landscape shade tree and also valued historically for timber.
disease_reason: Oak wilt, caused by Bretziella fagacearum, is a well-documented and highly destructive vascular disease affecting live oaks, particularly in Texas.
Leptographium spp. (e.g., L. terebrantis, L. procerum) are well-documented root-infecting fungi causing decline in loblolly pine, often associated with root-feeding bark beetles.
Needle rusts (e.g., Coleosporium spp.) do occur on loblolly pine, but the label names a broad disease category rather than a specific disease and lumps multiple pathogens together.

This labels a functional group of organisms (heart-rot/sap-rot basidiomycetes) rather than a specific disease, so it is too vague to serve as a disease class even though such fungi do colonize loblolly pine.
Leaf and flower gall caused by Exobasidium vaccinii is a well-documented disease of lowbush blueberry.
Hollyhock rust is caused by Puccinia malvacearum, which infects multiple Malvaceae hosts including common mallow (Malva spp.).

crop_notes: Cultivated for syrup production and timber.
disease_reason: Anthracnose caused by fungi such as Discula, Kabatiella, and Aureobasidium is a well-documented foliar disease of maples.

crop_notes: Cultivated for syrup production and timber.
disease_reason: Tar spot caused by Rhytisma acerinum and related species is a classic and widely recognized disease of maple leaves.

crop_notes: Cultivated for syrup production and timber.
disease_reason: Cankers of maple are real (e.g., Nectria, Eutypella, Steganosporium) but the label names a symptom/group rather than a specific disease.
Erwinia tracheiphila causes bacterial wilt in melon/cucurbits, vectored by cucumber beetles.

disease: Fusarium Wilts, Blights, Rots And Damping-Off
disease_reason: Combines multiple distinct Fusarium-caused syndromes into one vague umbrella label rather than naming a specific disease.
Monosporascus cannonballus causes a well-known root rot and vine decline of melon in hot climates.
Podosphaera xanthii and Golovinomyces cichoracearum are major foliar pathogens of melon.
Pseudoperonospora cubensis is a destructive foliar oomycete pathogen of melon.
Alternaria cucumerina causes a documented leaf blight of melon and other cucurbits.
Colletotrichum orbiculare causes anthracnose lesions on melon foliage and fruit.
Phytophthora capsici causes crown, fruit and foliar blight in melon.
Stagonosporopsis cucurbitacearum (Didymella bryoniae) is a major stem and foliar pathogen of melon.
Acidovorax citrulli causes fruit blotch on melon and other cucurbits, seed-borne.
Sour rot (Geotrichum candidum) is more typically reported on tomato/citrus; postharvest melon association exists but is uncommon and the label is ambiguous.
Macrophomina phaseolina causes charcoal rot/crown rot in melon under heat and drought stress.
Names a pathogen genus rather than a specific disease (damping-off, root rot, fruit rot) and overlaps with damping-off entry.

crop_notes: Microbiota decussata is a coniferous evergreen shrub grown ornamentally as a ground cover.
disease_reason: Phomopsis canker/twig blight is well-documented on many conifers (e.g., Juniperus), but specific verified reports on Microbiota decussata are sparse and the association is typically inferred from related Cupressaceae hosts.
Mimosa wilt is a well-documented vascular disease of Albizia julibrissin caused by the soilborne fungus Fusarium oxysporum f. sp. perniciosum.

Names the pathogen (Diplodia sapinea, syn. Sphaeropsis sapinea) rather than the disease it causes (Diplodia tip blight / Sphaeropsis shoot blight), though it is a well-documented pathogen of Mugo pine.

crop_notes: Rosa multiflora is an invasive wild shrub, not cultivated as an agricultural or horticultural crop.

disease_reason: Drippy blight is a documented bacterial disease (Lonsdalea quercina) affecting red oaks, especially Northern Red Oak, causing oozing cankers and dieback.
Names a fungal genus (Cryptocline, e.g., C. cinerescens causing leaf spot/anthracnose on oaks) rather than a specific disease, and the spelling/usage is informal.
Needle blight (caused by fungi such as Pestalotiopsis funerea, Phyllosticta thujae, and Kabatina thujae) is a well-documented foliar disease of Northern White Cedar (Thuja occidentalis).
Arborvitae is the common name for Thuja occidentalis (Northern White Cedar), so arborvitae needle blight directly refers to the same well-documented disease on this host.
Anthracnose caused by fungi such as Discula and Kabatiella is a well-documented foliar disease of Norway maple (Acer platanoides).
Cristulariella depraedans (zonate leaf spot) is a known foliar pathogen of Norway maple and other Acer species.
Rhizosphaera needle cast, caused by Rhizosphaera kalkhoffii, is a well-documented foliar disease of Norway spruce (Picea abies) and other spruces.
Ganoderma species (e.g., G. applanatum, G. lucidum) are well-documented causes of root and butt rot in oaks.
Names a broad fungal group rather than a specific disease; many polypores cause oak wood decay but the label is too vague.
Oak wilt, caused by Bretziella fagacearum, is a major vascular disease of oaks.
Bacterial leaf scorch caused by Xylella fastidiosa is a well-documented chronic disease of oaks.
Oak leaf blister caused by Taphrina caerulescens is a well-documented foliar disease of oaks.
Generic symptom-based label that does not specify pathogen; multiple fungi cause leaf spots on oak.
Botryosphaeria species cause documented cankers and dieback on oaks, especially stressed trees.
Coryneum twig blight is more commonly associated with stone fruits; its association with oak is unusual and poorly documented.
Cytospora cankers primarily affect conifers and hardwoods like poplar/willow; oak is an uncommon and weakly documented host.
Oak anthracnose caused by Apiognomonia (Discula) quercina is a well-documented foliar/twig disease.
Names a fungal genus rather than a disease; Monochaetia spp. are minor leaf-spot pathogens occasionally reported on oak.
Nectria canker (Neonectria spp.) is a documented canker disease of oaks and other hardwoods.

crop_notes: Oak lecanium (Parthenolecanium quercifex) is a scale insect pest of oak trees, not a plant or crop.

disease_reason: Crown rust, caused by Puccinia coronata f. sp. avenae, is the most economically important and well-documented foliar disease of oat worldwide.

crop_notes: Aesculus glabra, grown primarily as an ornamental/shade tree; nuts are toxic and not cultivated for food.
disease_reason: Rust is not a commonly documented disease of Ohio Buckeye (Aesculus glabra), which is far more typically affected by leaf blotch (Guignardia aesculi) and powdery mildew; the label is also vague without specifying a causal genus.
Choanephora cucurbitarum is a well-documented fungal pathogen causing wet rot of okra flowers and fruits, especially in warm humid conditions.
Downy mildew caused by Peronospora destructor is a well-documented and economically important foliar disease of onions.

Not a standard citrus disease name; likely a colloquial reference to whisker-like fungal growth (possibly Penicillium or Aspergillus post-harvest molds) rather than an established disease designation.
Downy mildew (caused by Plasmopara halstedii and related oomycetes) is a documented foliar disease of Rudbeckia fulgida (orange coneflower) and other Asteraceae.
Anthracnose caused by Colletotrichum species is a documented foliar and stem disease of Papaver orientale, producing characteristic sunken lesions.
Septoria petroselini causes a well-documented leaf spot disease on parsley, producing tan lesions with dark borders and pycnidia.
Brown rot caused by Monilinia fructicola/laxa is the most economically important fungal disease of peach worldwide.
Classic peach disease caused by Taphrina deformans, producing distorted reddened leaves.
Names a pathogen genus (Stigmina carpophila, cause of shot hole/Coryneum blight) rather than the disease itself.
Botryosphaeria canker does affect peach (gummosis/canker), but 'white rot' is typically an apple disease, making this combined label confusing for peach.
Peach mosaic virus (PcMV), transmitted by the peach bud mite, is a recognized viral disease of peach.
Names a fungal genus rather than a specific disease; Cladosporium carpophilum causes peach scab, but the label is too vague.
Well-documented soilborne disease of peanut caused by Sclerotium rolfsii (Athelia rolfsii).
This is the pathogen name (causal agent of late leaf spot of peanut), not a disease name — the disease should be labeled 'Late Leaf Spot'.
Refers to a fungal genus (former classification of the late leaf spot pathogen) rather than a specific peanut disease.
Pecan scab, caused by Venturia effusa (formerly Fusicladium effusum), is the most economically important disease of pecan.
Names a pathogen genus rather than a specific disease; Diplodia (e.g., Botryosphaeria/Diplodia spp.) can cause shuck dieback or twig dieback in pecan, but the label is vague.
Anthracnose caused by Colletotrichum spp. is a documented foliar and stem disease of peony.
Phytophthora cactorum is a well-known cause of crown and stem rot in peony, especially in poorly drained soils.
Botrytis paeoniae and B. cinerea cause the classic 'peony blight' affecting buds, stems, and leaves and are among the most common peony diseases.
Sclerotium rolfsii is a well-documented soilborne disease causing crown/stem rot on pepper.
Phytophthora capsici is one of the most economically important diseases of pepper worldwide.
TSWV (Orthotospovirus) is a major thrips-vectored virus of pepper causing ringspots and necrosis.
Well-known calcium-related physiological disorder affecting pepper fruit, analogous to tomato.
Xanthomonas euvesicatoria/spp. cause the major foliar/fruit bacterial disease of pepper.
Alternaria occurs on pepper as fruit rot and leaf spot, but 'Black Molds / Stem Cankers' is a vague compound label not standard for pepper.
Anthracnose (Colletotrichum spp.) is a major pepper fruit disease, but 'Bitter Rot' is the apple/grape name for Colletotrichum and combining them as one label is non-standard for pepper.
Powdery mildew (Erysiphe cichoracearum/Golovinomyces magnicellulatus) is the most common and well-documented disease of garden phlox.
Downy mildew caused by Peronospora phlogina is a documented foliar disease of Phlox species.
Real disease complex affecting phlox (caused by Rhizoctonia, Pythium, Phytophthora, Sclerotinia), but the label lumps multiple distinct diseases into one vague category.
Leaf and flower gall caused by Exobasidium vaccinii is a well-documented disease of azaleas including Piedmont azalea (Rhododendron canescens).

crop_notes: Quercus palustris; primarily grown as a landscape/shade ornamental tree, with minor timber use.
disease_reason: Drippy blight, caused by the bacterium Lonsdalea quercina in association with the kermes scale insect, is a well-documented disease specifically affecting pin oak (Quercus palustris).
Pine needle rusts caused by Coleosporium and related rust fungi are well-documented foliar diseases of pines.
This names the pathogen (Diplodia sapinea, syn. Sphaeropsis sapinea) with taxonomic authority rather than the disease name Diplodia tip blight or Sphaeropsis blight.
Ploioderma needle cast (Ploioderma lethale and related species) is a well-documented needle cast disease of pines, especially hard pines.

crop_notes: Combined entry for two distinct stone fruit crops (Prunus domestica and Prunus avium/cerasus); should be split into separate records.
disease_reason: Names a pathogen genus (Phloeosporella padi, the anamorph of Blumeriella jaapii) rather than a disease; corresponds to cherry leaf spot.

crop_notes: Combined entry for two distinct stone fruit crops (Prunus domestica and Prunus avium/cerasus); should be split into separate records.
disease_reason: Plum/cherry rust caused by Tranzschelia discolor is a well-documented disease of Prunus species.

crop_notes: Combined entry for two distinct stone fruit crops (Prunus domestica and Prunus avium/cerasus); should be split into separate records.
disease_reason: Black knot, caused by Apiosporina morbosa, is a major and well-known disease of plum and cherry.

crop_notes: Combined entry for two distinct stone fruit crops (Prunus domestica and Prunus avium/cerasus); should be split into separate records.
disease: Blumeriella Leaf Spot Of Cherry And Plum
disease_reason: Cherry leaf spot caused by Blumeriella jaapii is a well-established disease of cherry and plum.

crop_notes: Combined entry for two distinct stone fruit crops (Prunus domestica and Prunus avium/cerasus); should be split into separate records.
disease_reason: Brown rot, caused by Monilinia spp., is a major fruit and blossom disease of stone fruits including plum and cherry.

crop_notes: Combined entry for two distinct stone fruit crops (Prunus domestica and Prunus avium/cerasus); should be split into separate records.
disease_reason: Powdery mildew (Podosphaera spp.) is a documented foliar disease of cherry and plum.
Needlecast diseases (e.g., Elytroderma, Lophodermium, Lophodermella spp.) are well-documented foliar fungal diseases of Ponderosa pine causing needle discoloration and shedding.
Caused by Pectobacterium/Dickeya spp., a well-documented postharvest and field rot of potato tubers.
Phytophthora infestans late blight is the historically most devastating disease of potato.
Rhizoctonia solani causes black scurf, stem canker, and damping-off on potato.
Alternaria solani early blight is a common foliar disease of potato worldwide.

disease: Fusarium Wilts, Blights, Rots And Damping-Off
disease_reason: Fusarium dry rot and wilt do affect potato, but the label lumps multiple Fusarium syndromes into one vague genus-level entry rather than a specific disease.
Phytophthora erythroseptica (pink rot) affects potato, but 'root and stem rot' is the standard soybean-style label and is not the typical name used for potato Phytophthora disease.
TSWV is a documented thrips-transmitted virus of potato causing tuber necrosis and foliar symptoms.

crop_notes: Potato Dextrose Agar is a microbiological growth medium, not a plant or crop.

disease_reason: Names the pathogen (Thedgonia ligustrina, cause of privet leaf blotch/anthracnose-like spot) rather than the disease itself.

crop_notes: Ramp (Allium tricoccum) is a wild-harvested and increasingly cultivated North American leek used as a culinary vegetable.
disease_reason: Septoria species can cause leaf spots on various Allium and wild plants, but 'Septoria Leaf Spot And Cankers' on ramp (Allium tricoccum) is not a well-documented disease, and Septoria typically causes leaf spots rather than cankers.

crop_notes: Pinus resinosa, cultivated as a timber and ornamental conifer.
disease_reason: This names the pathogen (Diplodia sapinea, with taxonomic authority) rather than the disease, which is properly called Diplodia tip blight (or Sphaeropsis tip blight) of pines.

crop_notes: Pinus resinosa, cultivated as a timber and ornamental conifer.
disease_reason: Annosum root disease (Heterobasidion irregulare/annosum) is a well-documented and economically important root and butt rot of red pine, especially in thinned plantations.

crop_notes: Pinus resinosa, cultivated as a timber and ornamental conifer.
disease_reason: Sirococcus shoot blight (Sirococcus conigenus/tsugae) is a documented shoot blight affecting red pine and other conifers, particularly seedlings and saplings.

crop_notes: Redbay is a wild native tree of the southeastern US; not cultivated as an agricultural or horticultural crop.

disease_reason: Phyllosticta leaf spot is a documented fungal foliar disease affecting Enkianthus and related Ericaceae ornamentals.
Leaf blight (caused by fungi such as Drechslera/Helminthosporium and Pyrenophora spp.) is a well-documented foliar disease of reed canarygrass (Phalaris arundinacea).
Bitter rot (Colletotrichum spp.) is a disease of apples and other fruit crops, not a recognized disease of rhododendrons or azaleas.
Leaf and flower gall caused by Exobasidium vaccinii is a well-documented disease of azaleas and rhododendrons.

Guignardia leaf blotch is primarily associated with horse chestnut and other hosts; its association with rhododendrons/azaleas is unusual and the label names a pathogen genus rather than a standard disease name for this crop.

Pestalotiopsis can cause leaf spot/tip blight on rhododendrons, but the label names a pathogen genus rather than a standardized disease name and is often considered a secondary/opportunistic pathogen.
Well-documented disease of rice caused by Burkholderia glumae affecting panicles and grain fill.
Established rice disease caused by Cercospora janseana producing narrow brown lesions on leaves.
Major rice disease caused by Magnaporthe oryzae, one of the most economically damaging pathogens of rice worldwide.
Label conflates multiple distinct Rhizoctonia syndromes; sheath blight (R. solani) is the standard rice disease name rather than this generic grouping.
Powdery mildew caused by Podosphaera pannosa is a well-documented and common fungal disease of roses.
Black spot caused by Diplocarpon rosae is one of the most prevalent and damaging foliar diseases of roses worldwide.
Rose rosette disease, caused by Rose rosette emaravirus and vectored by an eriophyid mite, is a well-documented destructive viral disease of roses.

crop_notes: Saguaro is a wild desert cactus native to the Sonoran Desert, not cultivated as an agricultural or horticultural crop.

This names the pathogen (Diplodia sapinea) with its taxonomic authority rather than the disease it causes (Diplodia tip blight/Sphaeropsis blight).
Brown spot needle blight, caused by Lecanosticta acicola, is a well-documented foliar disease of Scots pine.
Sphaeropsis (Diplodia) tip blight and canker, caused by Sphaeropsis sapinea/Diplodia sapinea, is a major disease of Scots pine.
Anthracnose caused by Colletotrichum and related fungi is a well-documented foliar and fruit disease of Amelanchier (serviceberry).
Powdery mildew (notably Podosphaera species) is a common and well-documented foliar disease of serviceberry.

crop_notes: Common wild weed of the Brassicaceae family; occasionally foraged or used medicinally but not grown as an agricultural or horticultural crop.

disease_reason: Phytophthora species (notably P. cinnamomi) cause root rot in Shortleaf Pine and are implicated in littleleaf disease, the most damaging disease of this species.

crop_notes: Pinus monophylla, harvested for edible pine nuts.
disease_reason: Pinyon blister rust, caused by Cronartium occidentale, is a documented stem rust disease affecting singleleaf pinyon (Pinus monophylla) and other pinyon pines in the western US.

crop_notes: Soft scales are sap-sucking insect pests (Coccidae), not a plant or crop.
Solenostemon is an outdated genus name; the plant is now classified as Plectranthus scutellarioides, commonly known as coleus.
disease_reason: Downy mildew caused by Peronospora belbahrii (and related Peronospora spp.) is a well-documented disease of Solenostemon scutellarioides (coleus), causing leaf chlorosis, distortion, and defoliation.
Sclerotium rolfsii causes southern blight on soybean, especially in warm southern production regions.
Cercospora kikuchii causes Cercospora leaf blight and purple seed stain, a well-documented soybean disease.
Caused by Cercospora sojina, this is a major foliar disease of soybean worldwide.
BPMV is a Comovirus that infects soybean and is vectored primarily by bean leaf beetles.
Macrophomina phaseolina causes charcoal rot, a serious drought-associated soybean disease.
Phakopsora pachyrhizi causes Asian soybean rust, one of the most economically important soybean diseases.
Xylaria necrophora causes taproot decline, an emerging disease documented in the southern U.S. soybean belt.
Cadophora gregata (Phialophora gregata) causes brown stem rot, a well-known soybean disease.
SVNV is a Tospovirus widespread in U.S. soybean, transmitted by thrips.
Generic symptom-based label that could refer to Phytophthora, Pythium, Fusarium, or Rhizoctonia rather than one defined disease.
Pseudomonas savastanoi pv. glycinea causes bacterial blight, a common foliar disease of soybean.
Unusual name for soybean; Sclerotinia sclerotiorum on soybean is typically called Sclerotinia stem rot or white mold.
Septoria glycines causes brown spot (Septoria leaf spot), the most common foliar disease of soybean.
Names a pathogen genus rather than a disease; Diaporthe spp. cause pod and stem blight, stem canker, and Phomopsis seed decay on soybean.
Peronospora manshurica causes soybean downy mildew, a globally distributed foliar disease.
Rhizoctonia solani causes seedling damping-off, aerial blight, and root rot in soybean.
Xanthomonas axonopodis pv. glycines causes bacterial pustule, a recognized foliar disease of soybean.
Downy mildew caused by Peronospora effusa (P. farinosa f. sp. spinaciae) is the most economically important disease of spinach worldwide.
White rust of spinach caused by Albugo occidentalis is a well-documented oomycete disease, particularly significant in Texas and southern U.S. production.
Cladosporium leaf spot (Cladosporium variabile), also known as Cladosporium leaf spot or Heterosporium leaf spot, is a recognized fungal disease of spinach.

crop_notes: Euonymus europaeus, grown as an ornamental shrub/small tree; sometimes written as two words.
disease_reason: Powdery mildew (caused by Erysiphe euonymi-japonici and related Oidium species) is a well-documented and common foliar disease of Euonymus (spindletree) species.

crop_notes: This is an insect pest (Lymantria dispar), not a plant or crop.
Grown commercially as timber and as ornamental/Christmas trees.
disease_reason: Sirococcus shoot blight (Sirococcus conigenus/tsugae) is a well-documented shoot and tip blight affecting spruce species.

disease: Fusarium Wilts, Blights, Rots And Damping-Off
disease_reason: Fusarium spp. cause well-documented wilts, crown/fruit rots, and damping-off in squash.

Phytophthora capsici causes serious crown, fruit, and foliar blight on squash.
Choanephora cucurbitarum is a well-known cause of blossom-end and fruit rot in squash.
Caused by Stagonosporopsis cucurbitacearum (Didymella bryoniae); a documented cucurbit disease affecting squash.
Pseudoperonospora cubensis is a major downy mildew pathogen of cucurbits including squash.
Colletotrichum orbiculare causes anthracnose on cucurbits including squash.
Sclerotium rolfsii (Athelia rolfsii) causes southern blight on squash, especially in warm climates.
Pythium spp. cause damping-off and root rot in squash seedlings and mature plants.

crop_notes: Stenotaphrum secundatum; primarily cultivated as a warm-season turfgrass for lawns, also used as pasture forage.
disease_reason: Rhizoctonia solani causes large patch/brown patch and seedling damping-off in St. Augustinegrass, a well-documented turfgrass disease.

Botrytis cinerea is a major and well-documented disease of strawberry causing fruit and flower rot.

disease: Phomopsis Leaf Blight And Fruit Rot
disease_reason: Caused by Phomopsis obscurans, this is a recognized disease of strawberry affecting leaves and fruit.
Caused by Xanthomonas fragariae, this is a well-documented bacterial disease of strawberry.
Colletotrichum spp. cause anthracnose crown rot, fruit rot, and leaf spots in strawberry.
The label is vague — strawberry has multiple distinct leaf spot diseases (Mycosphaerella, Ramularia, Phomopsis, etc.) and the specific pathogen is unspecified.
Names the pathogen (with taxonomic authority) rather than the disease; the corresponding disease is common leaf spot of strawberry (Mycosphaerella fragariae / Ramularia tulasnei).

Pantoea species (e.g., P. ananatis) can cause leaf blight on sorghum and related grasses, but a distinct 'Pantoea rot and blight' is not a well-established named disease on Sudangrass and references the pathogen genus rather than a standardized disease name.
Erysiphe betae causes powdery mildew, a well-documented foliar disease of sugar beet worldwide.
BNYVV is the causal agent of rhizomania, a major economically important soilborne viral disease of sugar beet vectored by Polymyxa betae.
Caused by Cercospora beticola, this is the most damaging foliar disease of sugar beet globally.
Brown rot caused by Monilinia spp. is a major and well-documented disease of sweet cherry affecting blossoms and fruit.
Powdery mildew caused by Podosphaera clandestina is a well-known foliar and fruit disease of sweet cherry.
Scurf caused by Monilochaetes infuscans is a well-known sweet potato storage root disease.
Rhizopus stolonifer causes a classic soft rot of sweet potato storage roots.
'Bread mold' is a colloquial name (usually Rhizopus) and likely duplicates Rhizopus soft rot rather than a distinct disease.
Sclerotium rolfsii (southern blight) is documented on sweet potato.
Java black rot caused by Lasiodiplodia theobromae is a recognized postharvest disease of sweet potato.
SPFMV is a major, well-documented virus of sweet potato.
Sour rot (Geotrichum) is occasionally reported on sweet potato but is more commonly associated with other crops; association is uncommon.
Macrophomina phaseolina causes charcoal rot of sweet potato storage roots.
White rust (Albugo) affects crucifers, spinach, and ornamentals, not sweet potato.
Ceratocystis fimbriata black rot is a classic and historically important disease of sweet potato.
Bacterial wilt and soft rot (e.g., Ralstonia/Dickeya/Erwinia) are documented on sweet potato, though the label is broad.

Fusarium spp. cause root rot and wilt complexes in sweet potato.
Fusarium oxysporum f. sp. batatas causes Fusarium wilt (stem rot) of sweet potato.
Damping-off is more typical of seedling crops; sweet potato is propagated from slips, so this association is unusual and likely overlaps with Fusarium wilt/root rot.
Names a fungal genus rather than a disease; Penicillium causes only minor blue mold storage rot on sweet potato.
Pythium spp. cause root and stem rot (mottle necrosis) on sweet potato.
Streptomyces ipomoeae causes soil rot (pox), an important sweet potato disease.
Switchgrass rust, caused primarily by Puccinia emaculata, is a well-documented foliar disease of Panicum virgatum.
Rhizoctonia solani is a well-documented pathogen of tall fescue, causing brown patch (foliar blight), damping-off of seedlings, and root/crown rot.

CMV has a broad host range and regularly causes mosaic and shoestring symptoms on tomato.
Passalora fulva (Cladosporium fulvum) leaf mould is a major disease of greenhouse tomato.
Phytophthora infestans is the historically important late blight pathogen of tomato and potato.
Usually denotes Phytophthora capsici, which can infect tomato fruit/crown but the label overlaps in usage with Late Blight.
Pseudomonas syringae pv. tomato causes bacterial speck, a well-characterised tomato disease.
Ralstonia solanacearum (southern bacterial wilt) is a destructive vascular wilt of tomato.
TSWV is a thrips-transmitted tospovirus and a major virus disease of tomato.
Colletotrichum coccodes and related species cause anthracnose fruit rot on ripe tomato.
Septoria lycopersici is a classic foliar leaf spot of tomato.
Botrytis cinerea gray mold is a common disease of greenhouse and field tomato.
Rhizopus spp. cause post-harvest soft rot of tomato fruit.
Sclerotinia sclerotiorum 'timber rot' (white mold) is a recognised stem disease of tomato.
Duplicates 'Gray Mold' (Botrytis cinerea); pluralised label appears to be a near-identical entry.
Real disease (Ralstonia solanacearum) but duplicates 'Southern Bacterial Wilt' on tomato.
Verticillium dahliae/albo-atrum cause vascular wilt of tomato; pluralised label is acceptable since multiple species are involved.

Common name for Impatiens balsamina, grown as a garden ornamental; also applied to Mimosa pudica.

Not a standard tulip disease name; likely refers to Botrytis-related neck/bulb rot but the term is ambiguous and not a recognized formal disease designation for tulips.

Bacterial disease caused by Serratia marcescens affecting watermelon and other cucurbits.

Major watermelon disease caused by Acidovorax citrulli.
Well-documented watermelon disease caused by Phytophthora capsici.
Important watermelon disease caused by Stagonosporopsis cucurbitacearum.

Major wheat disease caused by Puccinia triticina.
Tilletia controversa disease of winter wheat stunting plants and replacing kernels with bunt balls.

Aphid-transmitted luteovirus that commonly infects wheat as well as barley and oats.
Puccinia striiformis f. sp. tritici causes yellow rust, a major wheat disease worldwide.
Pyrenophora tritici-repentis is a widespread foliar disease of wheat.
